See also: sociālista, sociālistā, and socialistă

Asturian

[edit]

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • socialiste (obsolete)

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /soθjaˈlista/ [so.θjaˈlis̪.t̪a]
  • Rhymes: -ista
  • Syllabification: so‧cia‧lis‧ta

Adjective

[edit]

socialista (epicene, plural socialistes)

  1. socialist
    • 1902 September 7, Francisco González Prieto “Xuan de les Portielles”, “Los Borregos Pastoriaos”, in Ixuxú, viva la mio quintana‎[1]:
      porque Pablo Iglesies y' un gran burgués que trata d'apoderase de les 80 agrupaciones socialistes d'España [...] Conque ya lo sabeis, obreros de Xixon, d'Asturies, d'España, 'nel VI Congresu Socialiste nacional celebrau los últimos dis d'agosto, 'nel qu' antes yera tiatru de Xovellanos...
      because Pablo Iglesias is a great bourgeois who tries to seize the 80 socialist groups of Spain [...] So you know now, workers of Gijón, Asturias, Spain, in the fourth national Socialist Congress celebrated the last days of august, in what used to be Jovellanos theater...

Noun

[edit]

socialista m or f (plural socialistes)

  1. socialist

Related terms

[edit]
  • socialismu

Further reading

[edit]
  • “socialista”, in Diccionariu de la llingua asturiana [Dictionary of the Asturian Language] (in Asturian), 1ª edición, Academia de la Llingua Asturiana, 2000, →ISBN

Latin

[edit]

Noun

[edit]

socialista m or f (genitive socialistae); first declension

  1. (New Latin) socialist
    • 1891, Pope Leo XIII, Rerum novarum:
      Ad huius sanationem mali Socialistae quidem, sollicitata egentium in locupletes invidia, evertere privatas bonorum possessiones contendunt oportere, earumque loco communia universis singulorum bona facere, procurantibus viris qui aut municipio praesint, aut totam rempublicam gerant.
      (please add an English translation of this quotation)

[edit]

First-declension noun.

singular plural
nominative socialista socialistae
genitive socialistae socialistārum
dative socialistae socialistīs
accusative socialistam socialistās
ablative socialistā socialistīs
vocative socialista socialistae

Portuguese

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From French socialiste (“socialist”). By surface analysis, social +‎ -ista.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • Rhymes: -istɐ
 
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /so.si.aˈlis.tɐ/ [so.sɪ.aˈlis.tɐ], (faster pronunciation) /so.sjaˈlis.tɐ/
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /so.si.aˈlis.tɐ/ [so.sɪ.aˈlis.tɐ], (faster pronunciation) /so.sjaˈlis.tɐ/
    • (Rio de Janeiro) IPA(key): /so.si.aˈliʃ.tɐ/ [so.sɪ.aˈliʃ.tɐ], (faster pronunciation) /so.sjaˈliʃ.tɐ/
    • (Southern Brazil) IPA(key): /so.si.aˈlis.ta/ [so.sɪ.aˈlis.ta], (faster pronunciation) /so.sjaˈlis.ta/
  • (Portugal) IPA(key): /su.sjɐˈliʃ.tɐ/

  • Audio (Brazil (Caipira)):(file)
  • Hyphenation: so‧ci‧a‧lis‧ta

Noun

[edit]

socialista m or f by sense (plural socialistas)

  1. (politics) socialist (one who practices or advocates socialism)
  2. (Portuguese politics) a member or supporter the Portuguese Socialist Party

Adjective

[edit]

socialista m or f (plural socialistas, not comparable)

  1. (politics) socialist (of, promoting, practising, or characteristic of socialism)
  2. (Portuguese politics) of or belonging to the Portuguese Socialist Party

Hyponyms

[edit]
  • comunista
  • estalinista
  • leninista
  • maoista
  • marxista
  • trotskista

[edit]
  • capitalista

Derived terms

[edit]
  • nacional-socialista

Related terms

[edit]
  • social
  • socialismo
  • socialistamente
  • sócio

Spanish

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /soθjaˈlista/ [so.θjaˈlis.t̪a] (Spain, Equatorial Guinea)
  • IPA(key): /sosjaˈlista/ [so.sjaˈlis.t̪a] (Latin America, Philippines)

Adjective

[edit]

socialista m or f (masculine and feminine plural socialistas)

  1. socialist
  2. (politics, Spain) Pertaining to PSOE (Partido Socialista Obrero Español), a Spanish political party

Noun

[edit]

socialista m or f by sense (plural socialistas)
